subject: Clarify: processing locality, subprocessor accountability, and deletion path
messages:
From: Alex Gonzalez <alex.gonzalez@medicore.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q — where exactly do requests from MediCore land?

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — impressed with the latency numbers. Before we move to an evaluation, Security has two quick clarifying questions around processing locality and deletion:

1) When our app calls the Redwood hosted API, which geographic regions could the inference requests touch (compute + any intermediate services)?
2) Which named subprocessors might see request payloads or cached KV material for a typical hosted plan? We need a roster (company names + country).
3) If a user requests data deletion, what is the end-to-end timeline and who is responsible for each step (Redwood runtime, cloud provider, subprocessor)? Is there an audit artifact we can rely on?

Would you be able to send a short map and roster we can include in the procurement review?

Best,
Alex
Director, Security — MediCore Health
[medicore logo]

From: avery_johnson@redwood.com
To: Alex Gonzalez <alex.gonzalez@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where exactly do requests from MediCore land?

Alex — great question.

High level answer up front: for our hosted (standard) offering, inference requests are executed in the cloud region you choose at the account level (we have US-West, US-East, EU-West, and APAC regions). If you select US-West for MediCore, execution and short-term KV cache are kept in the US regions listed below. However, control-plane metadata and some orchestration calls to billing/monitoring services may transit to our central control plane (US) for multi-region coordination.

Short bullets:
- Primary execution: US-West (oregon) — model weights and ephemeral GPU execution.
- KV/prefix cache: colocated in the same region for low-latency hits; short TTLs by default (configurable).
- Control-plane telemetry: routed to Redwood control plane (US) — we surface audit logs and traces for customers.
- Cross-border fallbacks: if US capacity is exhausted, policy can fail open (reject) or fail over to a pinned compatible variant in US-East. We do not fallback to EU/APAC without an explicit routing policy.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight execution map and our current subprocessor roster snapshot (names + country). See the attached files.

I'll put Connor and Marissa on the thread for the deletion/audit trace parts.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q — where exactly do requests from MediCore land?

Alex — quick follow-up on deletion accountability and evidence.

We break deletion into three stages:

1) Customer API/Control request: when MediCore calls the Delete API or triggers an erasure via the Console, we record a deletion request ID and timestamp. (Owner: MediCore)

2) Runtime purge: the runtime invalidates KV cache and queued inference contexts; ephemeral GPU memory is scrubbed on VM tear-down. TTL-driven cached artifacts (prefix cache) are removed within the configured TTL window; for forced erasures we accelerate the TTL. (Owner: Redwood runtime + cloud host)

3) Subprocessor deletion / confirmation: any long-term artifacts held by named subprocessors (e.g., managed logging provider, archival backups) are removed per the subprocessor contract timelines — typically 30 days for ours. We request and store deletion receipts from subprocessors into a customer-facing audit bundle. (Owner: Subprocessor — Redwood requests & verifies)

Evidence we provide:
- Deletion request ID and console audit trail (instant).
- Runtime purge confirmation events and timestamped log snippets (within 24 hours).
- Subprocessor deletion receipts (PDF) — aggregated into an evidence bundle; we aim to return that within 30 days.

A few important notes:
- We do not retain raw prompts or model outputs beyond configured retention unless you opt into longer telemetry retention for debugging.
- Backup snapshots are encrypted; erasure requests mark affected snapshots for exclusion on next rotation; physical destruction follows your retention policy schedule.
- For customers in regulated spaces we can offer a private deployment (VPC or Dedicated) to tighten subprocessor exposure and shorten SLA timelines.

Let me know if MediCore needs the subprocessor contract clauses (we can provide redacted SAs) or a signed attestation for procurement.

—Connor
Principal Product Manager, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of quick clarifications from Security after reviewing the map and roster:

• Can you confirm which subprocessor(s) are outside the US and whether any payloads (even transient logs) are routed to them? The roster lists two analytics partners in Ireland and one log-archival vendor in Singapore — we need to understand whether those vendors see request-level payloads or just aggregated telemetry.

• For the subprocessor deletion receipts: does Redwood push the receipts directly to the MediCore Console, or do you deliver them via secure email/drive only? We need receipts into our ticketing system (HubSpot ID HS-REC-56789).

If you can reply with a short yes/no per vendor and preferred receipt delivery mechanism, we can close procurement. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
Director, Security — MediCore Health
